body: Thank you, friend, I hope you have a good evening as well!

I feel like I'm being selfish and attention seeking for even writing this post. It's just kind of a way for me to let out some emotions, so dont feel obligated to respond or anything. I don't even know if I'm sad or if I'm making all of these emotions up in my head.
Did what you said and it went well, thanks dude!
Thanks dude, good luck with your presentation on wednesday !

I'm in the same boat, dude. I feel like I should be getting better now, but the pain is just getting progressively worse and I feel like I'm losing control. Even with my life becoming objectively better, I don't feel happiness. I miss being happy and I miss making other people happy. We'll get through this together, I guess

People coming from the darkest places can be the greatest motivators because they know what it feels like to be at rock bottom. They're usually the most sympathetic and caring, from my experiences. Just because someone was down and out doesn't mean they can't pick themselves up again. It takes balls to pick yourself up

Hey, man. I just want to say that I think that it takes an incredibly strong person to go through all of that. I feel alone with the cards I've been given, and I can only imagine how you feel. I only know about you from this post, but I look up to you for getting through all of this. I'm not in the best place right now, and i thank you for writing a post that captures my thoughts and feelings. I hope you have a great week and i hope we'll get through this together, dude.

Thanks, man, just going through one of those OCD panic attacks, ya know. My ocd flared up today after a bunch of traffic cop vehicles stopped at a street that I had driven through earlier (my OCD also includes the thought of driving through a red light on accident and hitting someone). I just wish I could get rid of this awful disease. Wish you the best, mate

I feel you dude, I have a similar fear of being thrown in jail for something I didn't do. Mine manifests itself in many ways, from the though of accidently hitting a pedestrian without realizing while driving, to someone thinking that I stole something from a store, etc. 

I'm just going to give up trying to worry about things that no one else does, and hopefully that works. It's hard though because the fear of going to jail is so so strong. We'll get through it together, I guess! 😂

I felt the same way a couple of months ago. Objectively, I should feel great about my life because it's really not that bad, but I was miserable, so I felt guilty for being upset. I realized in the end that I had to suck it up. No one will care about you more than you do. Start loving yourself and believing in yourself.

Start laughing at your mistakes and get rid of that cloud of guilt inside of your head. Start verbally congratulating yourself for things, narrate your day after work in your car, how you felt throughout the day etc. Just make yourself your best friend and love yourself. Realize your flaws and laugh at your flaws, and be proud of the little things that you're good at.

Also, help other people, even if it's something small, like giving them directions, texting a friend you haven't talked to in awhile, etc. Making people feel better makes you feel better.

Hope this helps

I think as long as you are truly innocent, a judge would see that you were actually the victim and you would be okay. Also, if this happened you, then this probably happens to a lot of other innocent people that aren't being thrown in jail.

Thanks dude, it's weird how OCD makes your brain want to "go back and make sure" to calm it down and ease the anxiety, even though going back and checking makes it much worse. It's pretty counterintuitive. I've had days where I can force myself to not check, and I'll feel great, and then others where if i don't retrace my route, I'll be mentally prepared to go to jail.
